The company, the product, the team and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the Scrum Master for a fictional team building a scheduling app for Brightwell Clinics. The last three Sprint Reviews were slide presentations to the Product Owner alone.
handover: Stakeholders (clinic managers, two front-desk leads) have never attended.
The Product Backlog has not changed after any Review.
howItWorks: The board shows the Sprint's commitments, the work, the impediments, the people's support and the Scrum events.
Move on a day at a time. A decision comes to you at each Daily Scrum; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Day 2: the team spends two days building slides for executives instead of working on the Sprint Goal.
Day 6: the rescheduling flow goes to clinics; desk staff take twice as long and revert to phone calls.
Day 10: the clinic managers decline the next Review: 'nothing we say changes anything'.

choices.label: With the Product Owner, invite the clinic managers and front-desk leads who will use the app, and explain the Review is where they help decide what's next
choices.feedback: The Sprint Review inspects the outcome with key stakeholders; without them it cannot adapt to their needs.

choices.label: Keep it to the Product Owner, who represents stakeholders
choices.feedback: Her view is valuable, but stakeholders never see or react to the product.

choices.label: Invite the clinic group's executives for a polished presentation
choices.feedback: It becomes a status presentation, not a working session.

choices.label: Replace slides with the working Increment: stakeholders try booking and rescheduling themselves while the team watches and takes feedback

effects.log: Front-desk leads find rescheduling takes too many steps.

choices.feedback: The Review is a working session: the team shows what it accomplished and stakeholders inspect and give feedback.

choices.label: Demo the Increment live, with questions at the end
choices.feedback: Better than slides, but stakeholders watch rather than use it.

choices.label: Present slides of completed items for sign-off
choices.feedback: Nobody touches the product; the rescheduling problem stays hidden.

adaptPrompt.title: Feedback with nowhere to go
adaptPrompt.context: Stakeholders asked for faster rescheduling and a waitlist.

choices.label: The Product Owner reorders the Product Backlog in the Review: faster rescheduling moves to the top, the waitlist is added, and a planned reporting feature drops

effects.log: The backlog changes with stakeholders present.

choices.feedback: The Product Backlog may be adjusted in the Review to meet new opportunities.

choices.label: Note the feedback for the Product Owner to consider later
choices.feedback: It may change the backlog, but stakeholders do not see their input acted on.

choices.label: Keep the backlog as planned; the roadmap is fixed
choices.feedback: The Review changes nothing, so stakeholders stop coming.

scoring.modelReasoning: The Sprint Review is a working session: the Scrum Team presents the results of its work to key stakeholders, who inspect the Increment, and the Product Backlog may be adjusted to meet new opportunities. Slides and sign-offs without stakeholders turn it into a status meeting.
